DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 57 s. 2022 June 30, 2022 Hon. RUBIO J. SINDON Punong Barangay Barangay Pulot Lagayan, Abra Dear Hon. Sindon. This refers to your Letter dated 19 February 2022 requesting from the Department, through the Office of Undersecretary for Barangay Affairs, a legal opinion on your Letter-Complaints against: (a) Hon. Edmarc L. Crisologo [Mayor Crisologo], Municipal Mayor of Lagayan, Abra; (b) Hon. Arnel A. Velasquez [SB Member Velasquez], Sangguniang Barangay Member and OIC Punong Barangay of Barangay Pulot; and (c) Landbank Bangued Office Branch Manager Gina Gabuat [LBP BM Gabuat]. Per the Letter and its attachments, this Department has culled the following material facts relevant to the inquiry: You are the duly-elected Punong Barangay of Barangay Pulot, Lagayan, Abra. On 05 March 2020, PB Sindon and your wife suffered multiple gunshot wounds inflicted upon by two (2) individuals in a motorcycle. You were rushed to Abra Provincial Hospital (Hospital) where you underwent abdominal surgery. You were confined in the Hospital from 05 to 13 March 2020. In a Letter dated IO June 2020, you were invited by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan (Sanggunian) for a legislative inquiry. The inquiry was in relation to your unauthorized absences since 13 March 2020, and his malfeasance in the distribution of relief goods and the Social Amelioration Program (SAP) funds during the COVID-19 pandemic. In your response dated 18 June 2020, you requested for the postponement of the legislative inquiry as his attending physician has not yet given him clearance to attend stressful activities. You likewise confirmed that the distribution of the relief goods was properly coordinated with the barangay officials, while the SAP funds was disseminated by SB Member Velasquez as the OIC, Office of the Punong Barangay. In the same letter, you questioned the authority of SB Member Velasquez to disseminate the SAP funds. SB Member Velasquez allegedly signed documents related to the funds prior to his appointment as OIC, Office of the PB. Hon. Apolinar Molina (Vice Mayor Molina) sent you another Letter dated 04 August 2020, with attached Resolution dated 17 July 2020 issued by the Sangguniang Page 1 of 9 "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

Barangay of Pulot, which alleged that (a) you failed to attend a number of barangay meetings without justifiable reason; (b) you did not reside in Barangay Pulot since your discharge from the hospital on 13 March 2020; and (c) your unauthorized absences caused unnecessary delay in the withdrawal of barangay funds at Landbank and the implementation of the Barangay's COVID-19 projects. You responded in a notarized letter dated 10 August 2020 stating that: 1. 2. 3. You confirmed that you failed to appear before a number of barangay meetings. Nonetheless, you constantly communicated with barangay officials, and gave directives affecting your constituents. You stated that after your discharge, you stayed near the hospital for your weekly check-ups. Nonetheless, you said that you did not leave the province of Abra. You reiterated that while you were discharged from the hospital by 13 March 2020, you have not yet fully recuperated from your injuries. As regards barangay funds, you stated that SB Member Velasquez has been withdrawing barangay funds, and even disseminated the SAP funds. At the end the notarized letter, you stated that you are not filing a leave of absence (LOA) as you will no longer be allowed to intervene in barangay affairs, and you do not want to abandon your constituents. On 15 November 2021, you submitted a Letter to Mayor Crisologo stating that you shall then resume your duties as the elected PB of Barangay Pulot. You attached a Medical Certificate dated 13 November 2021 stating that you are physically fit to work. Mayor Crisologo thus issued a Certification of Assumption to Duty dated 01 December 2021 in your favor. On 06 December 2021 , you sent LMB BM Gabuat a Letter informing her that you have officially returned as the PB of Barangay Pulot. You likewise asked to be the official signatory for all transaction related to your administration. On 09 December 2021, the Sangguniang Bayan of Lagayan, Abra held a special session to deliberate the Administrative Complaint against you, and concluded in an Order/Resolution, that: •"WHEREFORE, premises considered, it is hereby resolved to: a. b. c. d. e. Constitute the entire membership of the Sangguniang Bayan of Lagayan, Abra as the tribunal to hear and decide on the Administrative Complaint filed against RUBIO J. SINDON; Declare that there exists a Prima Facie case against RUBIO J. SINDON, in his capacity as Punong Barangay/Barangay Chairman; In relation to item b, this case shall now be captioned as, "In Re: Administrative Case against RUBIO J. SINDON, in his capacity as punong barangay/barangay chairman of Pulot, Lagayan, to be docketed as Administrative Case No. 2, Series of 2020, for the following charges: Violation of Section 60 paragraphs c and f of Republic Act No. 7160, otherwise known as the Local Government Code; Impose a period of SIXTY (60) days preventive suspension which shall commence upon notice to respondent of this Order/ResoIution; Allow the parties the option to submit a Position Paper/Memorandum, within FIFTEEN (15) days from receipt of a copy of this Resolution, which Position Paper shall be primarily on the main issue of whether or not RUBIO J. SINDON should be held Administratively liable, hence, should be imposed a penalty." Page 2 of 9 "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

The Administrative Complaint stems from your prolonged unauthorized absence from 13 March 2020 until 01 December 202.1 where you stayed outside your jurisdiction. Pending the investigation of the propriety of your justifications, the Sangguniang Bayan placed you under preventive suspension. You submitted your Position Paper to the Sangguniang Bayan on II December 2021 stating, in summary, that your prolonged absence was justified because: 1. Your absences were made in good faith and without malice. You believed that you and your family's lives were in danger and opted to move to a safer place; 2. At the height of the COVID-19 pandemic, you wanted to return to Barangay Pulot. Unfortunately, you were not allowed to enter the municipality due to COVID-19 restrictions; 3. SB Member Velasquez assumed the position of OIC, Office of the PB in your absence who faithfully discharged his duties; and 4. Mayor Crisologo authorized your return to office as per the Certification of Assumption to Duty. On 16 December 2021, you sent another Letter to LMB BM Gabuat requesting for the suspension of withdrawal of the barangay's Internal Revenue Allotment's until the internal conflict is solved. We summarize the issues as follows: (a) Whether the Sangguniang Bayan acted legal!y in the issuance of the Order/Resolution; (b) Whether Landbank should suspend the withdrawal of the monthly IRA of Barangay Pulot until the internal issues are resolved; and (c) Whether SB Member Velasquez had authority to sign the documents related to the distribution of SAP Funds prior to his appointment as OIC, Office of the Validity of the Order/Resolution We respectfully manifest that the assailed Order/Resolution imposing preventive suspension upon you is a valid exercise of the Sangguniang Bayan's quasi-judicial powers as granted under Republic Act No. 7160, or the Local Government Code (LGC). As such, this Department shall not interfere with the foregoing absent a clear violation of the law. We bring your attention to DILG Legal Opinion No. 12, series of 2009 wherein the same issue was presented before this Department. In the said opinion, this Department held that: "In reply thereto, please be informed that this Department is bereft of any authority to declare invalid or illegal any legislative measure passed by local sanggunians such . as the Barangay Bayan Resolution No. 2008-048 recommending a sixty (60) days suspension against PB Fabunan enacted by the Sangguniang Bayan, that Municipality. Only courts can make such declaration upon filing of a proper action before the forum. Similarly, in DILG Legal Opinion No. 23, series of 2011, this Department held that: Page 3 Of 9 "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

"Based on the facts already presented, we hereby clarify that the Legal Opinion signed by Atty. delos Santos merely reiterated the well-settled rule that the determination of the conditions upon which preventive suspension may be imposed under the law is vested exclusively with the sanggunian concerned. On the basis of DILG Legal Opinion No. 41, s. 2009, citing DILG Legal Opinion No. 38 s. 2003, the main reason for the rule is that since the disciplining and investigating authority over erring barangay and municipal/component city elective officials is the Sangguniang Bayan/Sangguniang Panlungsod and the Sangguniang Panlalawigan, respectively, it follows therefore that the sanggunian concerned has the sole power and discretion to determine whether or not preventive suspension so warrants against the respondent. Preventive suspension is thus said to be an incident to jurisdiction and/or tool for the disciplining authority, that is, the sanggunian concerned, to make use in the course of its administrative investigation." We note that preventive suspension is not the final determination of an elective officiål's administrative case. It is merely a tool which may be used by the Sanggunian concerned to aid them in investigating the allegations against the official concerned. Rest assured, the drafters of the LGC have included adequate safeguards so as not to allow the abuse the power of imposing preventive suspension, which we reiterate below: Section 63. Preventive Suspension. - (a) Preventive suspension may be imposed: xxxx (b) Preventive suspension may be imposed at any time after the issues are joined, when the evidence of guilt is strong, and given the gravity of the offense, there is great probability that the continuance in office of the respondent could influence the witnesses or pose a threat to the safety and integrity of the records and other evidence: Provided, That, any single preventive suspension of local elective officials shall not extend beyond sixty (60) days: Provided, further, That in the event that several administrative cases are filed against an elective official, he cannot be preventively suspended for more than ninety (90) days within a single year on the same ground or grounds existing and known at the time of the first suspension. . (c) Upon expiration Of the preventive suspension, the suspended elective official shall be deemed reinstated in office without prejudice to the continuation of the proceedings against him, which shall be terminated within one hundred twenty (120) days from the time he was formally notified of the case against him. However, if the delay in the proceedings of the case is due to his fault, neglect, or request, other than the appeal duly filed, the duration Of such delay shall not be counted in computing the time of termination of the case. (d) Any abuse of the exercise of the power of preventive suspension shall be penalized as abuse of authority. Section 64. Salary of Respondent Pending Suspension. - The respondent official preventively suspended from Office shall receive no salary or compensation during such suspension; but upon subsequent exoneration and reinstatement, he shall be paid full salary or compensation including such emoluments accruing during such suspension." Authority of SB Member Velasquez to siqn SAP documents Page 4 of 9 "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline NO.: 8876-34-54

This Department submits its position that SB Member Velasquez is authorized to sign the documents related to SAP even prior to the issuance of his appointment docurnents as the acting Punong Barangay of Pulot. The relevant provisions of the LGC are as follows: Section 46. Temporary Vacancy in the Office of the Local Chief Executive. - (a) When the governor, city or municipal mayor, or punong barangay is temporarily incapacitated to perform his duties for physical or legal reasons such as, but not limited to, leave of absence, travel abroad, and suspension from office, the vice-governor, city or municipal vice-mayor, or the highest ranking sangguniang barangay member shall automaticallv exercise the powers and perform the duties and functions of the local chief executive concerned, except the power to appoint, suspend, or dismiss employees which can only be exercised if the period of temporary incapacity exceeds thirty (30) working days. (b) Said temporary incapacity shall terminate upon submission to the appropriate sanggunian of a written declaration by the local chief executive concerned that he has reported back to office. In cases where the temporary incapacity is due to legal causes, the local chief executive concerned shall also submit necessary documents showing that said legal causes no longer exist. (c) When the incumbent local chief executive is traveling within the country but outside his . territorial jurisdiction for a period not exceeding three (3) consecutive days, he may designate in writing the officer-in-charge of the said office. Such authorization shall specify the powers and functions that the local official concerned shall exercise in the absence of the local chief executive except the power to appoint, suspend, or dismiss employees. (d) In the event, however, that the local chief executive concerned fails or refuses to issue such authorization, the vice-governor, the city or municipal vice-mayor, or the highest ranking sangguniang barangay member, as the case may be, shall have the right to assume the powers, duties, and functions of the said office on the fourth (4th) day of absence of the said local chief executive, subject to the limitations provided in subsection (c) hereof. (e) Except as provided above, the local chief executive shall in no case authorize any local official to assume the powers, duties, and functions of the office, other than the vice- governor, the city or municipal vice-mayor, or the highest ranking sangguniang barangay member, as the case may be. This Department further expounded the foregoing provision in its Memorandum Circular No. 2019-21 with subject "Operational Guidelines and Rules in Implementing Administrative Order No. 15 Series Of 2018" which states: "A. Temporary Vacancy in the Office of the Local Chief Executive (LCE) • Vacancy in general, according to prevailing jurisprudence, presupposes a situation when there is no person lawfully authorized to assume and exercise at present the duties of the office. LCEs pertain to governors, city mayors, municipal mayors and punong barangays. There is a temporary vacancy in the office of the governor, city mayor, municipal mayor or punong barangay if he/she is temporarily incapacitated to perform his duties for physical or legal reasons such as, but not limited to, leave of absence, travel abroad, and suspension from office. Page 5 of 9 "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No. : 8876-34-54

4. When a temporary vacancy exists in the office of the punong barangay, the first ranking sangguniang barangay member or in case of his/her inability, the second highest ranking sangguniang barangay member shall automatically exercise the powers and perform the duties and functions of the punong barangay, except the power to appoint, suspend, or dismiss employees which can only be exercised if the period of temporary incapacity exceeds thirty (30) working days." We note, on the outset, that you mentioned that upon his temporary absence, SB Member Velasquez became the "OIC-PB" of Barangay Pulot. Based on the Letter, however, we deem the nature of SB Member Velasquez's service as "acting PB", not OIC-PB. Under the LGC, an OIC local chief executive (LCE) is designated only when the incumbent local chief executive is traveling within the country but outside his territorial jurisdiction for a period not exceeding three (3) consecutive days. The acting LCE, on the other hand, is automatically designated upon the incumbent LCE's temporary incapacity. The powers and functions of the OIC LCE is limited to the authorization issued by the incumbent LCE; while an official in an acting capacity automatically exercise the powers and perform all the duties and functions of the LCE concerned, except the power to appoint, suspend, or dismiss employees which can only be exercised if the incumbent LCE's temporary incapacity exceeds thirty (30) working days. The foregoing distinction between an officer in an "OIC capacity" and an "acting capacity" was discussed in DILG Legal Opinion No. 02, series of 2018 to wit: "Anent your query, before we answer the same, it is worthy to know first the distinction of an "Acting Capacity" and an "Officer-in-charge" (OIC). In Resolution No. 0007778 dated 24 March 2000, issued by the Civil Service Commission (CSC), re: "Distinction between Acting and OIC'", it was pointed out that: 'It must be noted that a designation under acting capacity may be differentiated from a designation as Officer-in-Charge (OIC) in such a manner that an OIC enjoys limited powers which are confined to functions of administration and ensuring that the office continues its usual activities. The OIC may not be deemed to possess the power to appoint emptoyees as the same involves the exercise of discretion which is beyond the power of an OIC. On the other hand, as aptly ruled by the Commission in the case of Amado S. Day, a designation in an acting capacity entails not only the exercise of the ministerial functions attached to the position but also the exercise of discretion." "The designation of an OIC is nothing more than a temporary and convenient arrangement intended to avert paralyzation of the day to day operations of an office in the meantime that the chief or head of office is temporarily absent." Based on your Letter, you were temporarily incapacitated due to medical reasons caused by two (2) unscrupulous men. You did not appoint any official in an OIC capacity to temporarily fill his position. SB Member Velasquez was therefore designated as the acting PB, not OIC FB. Based on the foregoing, the acting punong barangay shall automatically have the authority to perform all the duties and powers pertaining to the Office of the Barangay Page 6 of 9 "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

Captain. The only limitation refers to the power to appoint, suspend, or dismiss employees which have additional qualifications as stated above. Verily, when SB Member Velasquez assumed the position of acting PB, he became imbued with the powers of the Office of the Punong Barangay which includes,• among others, the power to approve vouchers related to the disbursement of barangay funds. 1 Release of Internal Revenue Allotments by Landbank This Department cannot accede to the request of PB Sindon concerning the suspension of Barangay Pulot's monthly IRA withdrawals from Landbank. Under the Commission on Audit (COA) Manual of Financial Management for Barangays (Manual) prescribed under COA Circular No. 2015-11, the punong barangay has the following fiscal responsibilities: 12.1 Fiscal Responsibilities of Barangay Officials .1n connection with the management of the barangay funds and property, the duties and responsibilities of the barangay officials are as follows: 121.1 Punong Barangay In coordination with the barangay development council, prepares the annual a. executive and supplemental budgets of the barangay; Implements function, project contracts and activities to provide basic services and b. facilities to the barangay as appropriated; Negotiates, enters into and signs contracts for and in behalf of the barangay upon c. authorization of the SB; Certifies DVS and payrolls as to validity, propriety and legality of the claim; d. Approves claims relating to the disbursements of barangay funds; e. Countersigns checks in payment of the claims; f. Prepares the PB Certification for barangay check disbursements per COA g. Circular No. 2012-005 dated December 7, 2012. Signs the Statement Of Management Responsibility over the Financial h. Statements; Ensures that all transaction documents and reports are submitted to the CIM accountant; Keeps complete records on the buildings and other structures of the barangay; Conducts physical count of supplies, investment property, property, plant and k. equipment, and biological assets; Ensures that all accounting documents and records are properly kept by concerned barangay officials and staff; and m. Informs the COA Auditor's Office of the resignation, retirement, suspension of the barangay officials including change of BT so that the latter could be subjected to audit. As stated previously, the acting PB shall have authority to conduct all functions of the Office of the Punong Barangay, except for the power of appointment which requires compliance with additional factors. This includes the fiscal responsibilities of the punong barangay, such as approval of disbursements and checks, among others. Local Government Code, Section 389(b)(6). Page 7 of 9 "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

Verily, SB Member Velasquez, as the acting PB is duly authorized to handle the barangay's funds in Landbank for the conduct of projects and activities within Barangay Pulot. Your request to suspend the withdrawal of barangay funds may have the unintentional effect of haltering barangay services and, ultimately, affect the delivery of basic services to his constituents. The •foregoing pronouncement is without prejudice to the requirements set by Landbank for the withdrawal of Barangay Pulot's funds in accordance with the Supreme Court's pronouncement in Olama vs. PNB2, which states: "From the foregoing, it is not correct to say, as petitioners claimed, that the refusal Of the respondent PNB to release the IRA is unjustified. PNB has the right to require petitioners to present the proper certification as duly elected punong barangays from the Local Government Operations Officer of Tubaran, Lanao del Sur. Since the latter did not issue the certifications to the petitioners, there must be compelling reasons for such refusal as shown in the foregoing discussion." Lastly, may we respectfully inform you that the term "internal revenue" has been changed to "shares in national taxes" or "national tax allotment shares" in consonance with the ruling of the Supreme Court in the Mandanas-Garcia case. This opinion is rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have sufficiently addressed your concerns. Thank you. Very-truly yours, BY AUT F THE SECRETARY: B. DIN d ecretary for Barangay Affairs BAIMBD/LLLS/LRALLD/kuq/clp Encl: Letter dated 19 February 2022 from Hon.
